hypothesis: For three fixed orthogonal chambers and two equal-width necks, exact source/target phase matching succeeds when both necks grow with an irrational limiting length ratio. Possible asymptotic failures reduce to finitely many bounded-denominator rational ratios determined by a fixed middle transit beam.
missing_implication: Handle simultaneous divergent neck parameters without treating one growing side as fixed; retain exact endpoint images and intermediate phase.
success_criterion: Prove the all-parameter sequence statement with rigorous middle first-transit beam, exact sign/period bookkeeping and elementary robust rotation-net lemma; otherwise identify exact countermechanism.
strongest_objection: Independent local beams may be incompatible under target-phase rigidity (A17); arbitrary phase orbits and changing ratio cannot be treated as automatically dense.
scope: Exactly three fixed orthogonal chambers, two straight horizontal equal-width necks, actual opposing fixed interior marks; no general room decomposition or diagonal extension.
kind: Bounded hand proof synthesis; no room/ray/direction/word discovery, no implementation beyond proof receipts
